documents.title: H&P - Admission, Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive leg swelling and breathlessness x 5 days.
HPI:
89 yo male with HFrEF (EF 30-35% per prior cardiology records), CKD3a, HTN, permanent AFib on apixaban, presents with worsening dyspnea and edema.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Reports sleeping in recliner x 3 nights, 3-pillow orthopnea, two episodes of nocturnal dyspnea waking him at 02:00.
Respiratory rate 20; reports shortness of breath climbing one flight of stairs; comfortable at rest.
Denies chest pain, fever, cough, hemoptysis, syncope. Appetite poor. No recent diet indiscretion per daughter, though she notes canned soup at lunch most days.
Daughter checks his weights on a home scale most mornings; last recorded 92.1 kg.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
Furosemide 40 mg IV given once in the ED with good urine output; switched to home oral dose the next morning.
Documented 900 mL out in ED over 3 h with symptomatic improvement.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
HFrEF, ischemic cardiomyopathy. AFib, rate controlled. HTN. CKD stage 3a, baseline Cr 1.5. BPH. Remote cholecystectomy.
No prior intubation. No ICD.
HOME MEDICATIONS:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID (recently doubled from 40 mg BID)
Carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily
Apixaban 2.5 mg PO BID
Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO nightly
SOCIAL:
Lives with daughter in a first-floor apartment. Uses a rollator. Former smoker, quit >30 yrs, 20 pack-yr. No alcohol.
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash.
EXAM at 22:40:
T 36.6, HR 88 irregular, BP 112/64, RR 20, SpO2 91% on 4L NC. Wt 96.6 kg.
Gen: elderly, thin, speaking in full sentences, mildly anxious.
HEENT: JVP elevated approx 12 cm at 45 deg.
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, S3 present, no murmur appreciated, PMI displaced laterally.
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid-scapula, no wheeze. Breathing eased with head of bed up.
Abd: soft, nontender, liver edge 2 cm below costal margin.
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid-thigh bilaterally, scrotal edema, warm, cap refill 2 s at this time.
Skin: chronic venous stasis changes both shins, no ulceration.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit.
LABS:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
WBC 7.4, Hgb 11.2, Plt 188.
Trop-I 0.04 -> 0.04 (flat). TSH pending. Mg 1.9. Alb 3.3.
LFTs: AST 32, ALT 28, T bili 1.2.
EKG: atrial fibrillation at 92, LBBB, no acute ST change, unchanged from prior tracing on file.
ASSESSMENT:
89 yo male with acute decompensated HFrEF, volume overloaded, hypoxemic, despite recent outpatient diuretic escalation. Picture is congestive rather than infectious - no fever, no leukocytosis.
Etiology likely dietary sodium plus progression of underlying cardiomyopathy; renal function limits oral diuretic absorption in the setting of gut edema.
PLAN:
1. Admit to telemetry. Strict I/O, daily standing weights at 06:00.
2. IV loop diuresis, transition to home oral dose in AM per ED plan; goal net negative 1-1.5 L/day.
3. O2 to keep SpO2 >90%, wean as tolerated.
4. Hold sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone tonight given Cr 1.7; recheck BMP at 05:00.
5. Continue carvedilol at home dose while perfusion adequate.
6. Continue apixaban. 2 g sodium, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
7. Cardiology consulted, will see in AM.
8. Code status: full, confirmed with pt and daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Slept better, 2 pillows. Voided frequently overnight, used urinal x 6. Denies chest pain. Still breathless with bathroom walk.
Net -1,650 mL overnight. Weight down 1.8 kg to 94.8 kg.
Furosemide 40 mg IV given once in the ED with good urine output; switched to home oral dose the next morning.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.4, HR 84 irreg, BP 104/62, RR 20 at rest, SpO2 92% on 4L NC at 07:15.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2. Trial off O2 at 08:00 dropped him to 88%, back on 4L.
Respiratory rate 20; reports shortness of breath climbing one flight of stairs; comfortable at rest.
JVP approx 9 cm. Crackles now lower third only. Edema 2+ to knees, scrotal edema improved.
Extremities warm this morning, cap refill <3 s.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL) - not repeated today.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
Acute decompensated HFrEF, diuresing appropriately, Cr up modestly to 1.8 - expected with decongestion, watch trend.
1. Resume home oral furosemide this AM as above; reassess response at 14:00.
2. KCl 40 mEq PO x1 for K 3.6.
3. Continue holding sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone.
4. Continue carvedilol 6.25 BID; monitor BP, soft at 104/62.
5. O2 4L NC, wean as SpO2 allows. Out of bed to chair with PT.
6. Daily weight, strict I/O, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
7. Cardiology to round this afternoon.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon, Acute Hypotension
lines: EVENT NOTE / AFTERNOON ROUNDS:
Called by RN at 15:20 for hypotension and confusion. Pt drowsy but rousable, says he feels "washed out," no chest pain.
BP 84/52, cool mottled extremities; dobutamine started at 2.5 mcg/kg/min as inotrope support.
HR 96 irregular, RR 20, SpO2 91% on 4L NC, T 36.2.
Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2 - no escalation of O2 needed during event.
Exam: JVP still approx 9 cm, S3 persists, crackles at bases, knees down cool and mottled, cap refill 4-5 s, radial pulses thready.
Urine output fell to 20 mL/h over prior 2 h.
Lactate 2.6. Repeat BMP: Na 135, K 3.9, BUN 46, Cr 2.0. Trop-I 0.05, flat.
EKG at 15:35: AFib 98, LBBB, no new ischemic change.
ASSESSMENT:
Low cardiac output state / cardiogenic pattern in setting of aggressive decongestion plus beta blockade. Not hypovolemic by JVP. No evidence of infection - afebrile, WBC normal.
PLAN:
1. Continue dobutamine, titrate to MAP >65 and improved perfusion; no further titration needed so far.
2. Hold carvedilol.
3. Hold diuretic dose this evening; reassess at 20:00.
4. Cardiology at bedside, agrees with plan, favors short inotrope course and re-decongestion once perfusion restored.
5. Hourly UOP, q1h vitals, arterial line deferred as cuff pressures tracking.
6. Continue apixaban; Cr trend followed.
7. Transfer to step-down for closer monitoring.
19:40 addendum: BP 102/60, extremities warmed, cap refill 2 s, UOP 70 mL/h. Dobutamine weaning, plan off tonight. Mentation back to baseline, joking with daughter.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Acute Decompensated HFrEF
lines: ADMIT/DISCHARGE: Admitted HD1, discharged HD3.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute decompensated heart failure with reduced EF, congestive phenotype
2. Transient low output state requiring brief inotrope support
3. Acute kidney injury on CKD 3a, resolving
4. Permanent atrial fibrillation on apixaban
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:

89 yo male presented with 5 days of worsening dyspnea and edema. Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2. Weaned to room air HD3 at 08:00 with SpO2 93% at rest and 91% after hallway walk.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Furosemide 40 mg IV given once in the ED with good urine output; switched to home oral dose the next morning.
HD2 afternoon he became hypotensive: BP 84/52, cool mottled extremities; dobutamine started at 2.5 mcg/kg/min as inotrope support. Carvedilol and diuretic held.
Perfusion restored within hours; dobutamine off by 22:00 HD2 with BP 106/64 sustained off support.
HD3 he was warm, alert, ambulating with rollator. Diuretic resumed at reduced oral dose. Cr peaked 2.0, down to 1.8 at discharge.
Total net negative 2.9 L; weight 92.7 kg at discharge from 96.6 kg on admission.
Respiratory rate 20; reports shortness of breath climbing one flight of stairs; comfortable at rest.
DISCHARGE EXAM:
T 36.5, HR 78 irreg, BP 108/66, RR 20, SpO2 93% RA. JVP approx 7 cm. Bases clear to mid-lung. 1+ edema at ankles. Extremities warm.
DISCHARGE LABS: Na 136, K 4.1, HCO3 27, BUN 40, Cr 1.8, Hgb 11.0.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Furosemide 40 mg PO BID (reduced from 80 mg BID)
Carvedilol 3.125 mg PO BID (reduced; hold if SBP <95)
Apixaban 2.5 mg PO BID - continue
Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO nightly
Sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone HELD at discharge; cardiology to restart based on renal function and BP.
INSTRUCTIONS:
Daily morning weight on home scale; call for gain of 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week.
2 g sodium diet, 1.5 L fluid limit. Avoid canned soups - reviewed with daughter.
Call for lightheadedness, weight gain, increasing leg swelling, or new breathlessness at rest.
FOLLOW-UP:
Cardiology clinic in 5 days with BMP drawn prior.
Home nursing for weights, vitals, and medication review, 2 visits in first week.
Discharged to home with daughter, ambulating with rollator, room air, no oxygen at home.
